text:
maria-support: Customer (Acme) reporting partial chat streaming — responses arrive, then stall mid-sentence ~20-40s, then remaining tokens appear. Happening on hosted API (us-west). Request ID: req_20260317_9b7f23. Repro on their app and curl. @oliver can you triage?

oliver-engineer: ack. first pass: is this SSE or websocket? any client logs / HAR?

acme-dev: it's EventSource (SSE) in a React app. We see browser console show no network disconnects. HAR attached in ticket. Also saw `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` then long silence.

kai-frontend: common cause is client-side buffering when using fetch polyfills or proxies. Which polyfills? Are they using a service worker or nginx reverse-proxy?

acme-dev: no service worker. They go through our CDN (fastly). Using native EventSource in Chrome 112.

sebastian-sre: can we get the raw server-side streaming logs for that request ID? timeline of chunk flushes (content-length / chunked chunks) would help.

maria-support: forwarded request id and session id to infra. Also: user reports this happens intermittently under load.

oliver-engineer: infra says server emitted chunked frames at 14:23:12, 14:23:13, then nothing until 14:23:35 when remainder sent. So server output seems bursty. Need to check internal batching/kv-cache flush.

sebastian-sre: possible causes: (1) server-side batching thresholds delayed flush (2) kernel Nagle interactions on our edge (3) CDN buffering. Let's try repro with a curl SSE client that keeps connection open and prints chunk arrival times.

oliver-engineer: repro curl (run from outside CDN):

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream?model=gpt-4r&request_id=req_20260317_9b7f23" --verbose --no-buffer
```

oliver-engineer: `-N` + `--no-buffer` shows chunks as they arrive. If you see long gaps here, server is delaying. If curl shows steady stream but browser doesn't, likely CDN/client buffering.

acme-dev: ran curl from their laptop, saw same pauses. So server is likely delaying. Attached curl output with timestamps.

kai-frontend: can you also capture a raw TCP capture (pcap) between client and CDN or run curl from a machine in same subnet as the client? helps differentiate CDN buffering.

sebastian-sre: infra: please share the backend worker logs for that req_id and the internal queue timestamps (enqueue, start_generate, flush_token). Also include any kernel-level TCP stats around time.

support-bot: debug bundle created: dbg_20260317_9b7f23 — contains request headers, worker logs (rolling 5m), and routing metadata. Link: https://internal.redwood/debug/dbg_20260317_9b7f23

maria-support: asking customer to run curl example and share timestamps + whether curl run from behind same CDN. Also asked for browser HAR export and their CDN logs.

acme-dev: provided HAR and Fastly edge logs: shows edge accepted streaming from origin at 14:23:12 but held data until 14:23:34, then flushed. Fastly indicates 'small-chunk-coalescing' on by default.

oliver-engineer: that points to CDN buffering. Two options: (A) enable streaming-friendly headers (e.g., `Cache-Control: no-transform` and flush small chunks with `X-Accel-Buffering: no` or `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` + periodic zero-length flush) (B) ask customer to connect directly to origin bypassing CDN for testing.

oliver-engineer: server-side we can also reduce internal flush threshold: set `stream_flush_interval_ms` from 250ms -> 50ms for this route temporarily. Will patch on canary and test.

sebastian-sre: rolling change: applied lower flush interval to canary pool at 14:40. Can we reproduce after canary?

acme-dev: after canary change, curl shows steady token arrival. Browser via CDN still shows coalesced chunks.

kai-frontend: confirms: when CDN sits in front, even with origin sending many small chunks, Fastly coalesces into larger packets unless you add `Surrogate-Control: no-store` / or set `Cache-Control: no-transform`. Customer should set `Cache-Control: no-transform` on the streaming endpoint responses.

maria-support: told customer to add `Cache-Control: no-transform` header or bypass CDN for streaming endpoints. Also offered to keep canary flush change if helpful.

acme-dev: will test with Cache-Control change and report back. thanks! :tada:

oliver-engineer: noted for docs: add a troubleshooting blurb about CDN buffering + suggested headers and curl repro steps. I'll open a short doc PR.

maria-support: closing loop in ticket once customer confirms.

sebastian-sre: follow-up action items: ["document CDN headers for streaming" , "monitor stream_flush_interval effects on throughput" , "add a debug flag to dump chunk timing to debug bundle"]

maria-support: thanks team — good cross-checks.
